_meta.purpose: Constants/magic-bytes used by ransomware crypto code. Found in .rdata or computed at startup.
sources: Bouncy Castle / OpenSSL EVP_KDF / NIST SP 800-108 (KDF)
Crypto++ cryptlib.h public API (well-known public class/method names)
MITRE ATT&CK T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact) - public reference
Microsoft CNG / BCrypt / WinCrypt public API documentation (learn.microsoft.com)
NTRU / Kyber / NIST PQC public references
OpenSSL public headers (evp.h, aes.h, rsa.h, chacha.h, ec.h, kdf.h) - well-known public API

Public reverse-engineering literature on ransomware families (Sodinokibi/REvil, Conti, LockBit, BlackCat/ALPHV, Babuk, DarkSide, Maze, Ryuk, Phobos, GandCrab, Hermes, Petya, NotPetya, BadRabbit, Cerber, Globe, Stop/Djvu, Avaddon, Snake, Egregor, Avos, Hive, BlackByte)
libsodium public API documentation (doc.libsodium.org) - crypto_* function index
_meta.consolidation_note: Merged constants[] + self_prng_indicators[] + hardcoded_key_indicators[] previously living in crypto_signatures_extended.json (now retired) so all byte-magic detection data lives in one file. Also merged RSA padding constants + EVP_KDF_fetch name strings from the retired openssl_symbols.json (2026-05-20).

history.label: C5FIX
history.note: Applied 12 CRITICAL crypto-constants corrections (serpent_phi, rc6_p32, sha384_iv, aes_te0/td0, twofish q0/q1, petya->verification_fill, darkside_footer quarantine, babuk_marker !!, pem_rsa label, calg_des).

constants.name: sha256_iv
constants.description: SHA-256 initial hash values H0..H7 (eight 32-bit words derived from the fractional parts of the square roots of the first 8 primes).

constants.name: sha512_iv
constants.description: SHA-512 initial hash values H0..H7 (eight 64-bit words from the fractional parts of the square roots of the first 8 primes).
constants.spec_citation: NIST FIPS 180-4 Sec 5.3.5 (SHA-512 initial hash values H0..H7)
constants._note: Regenerated from NIST FIPS 180-4 canonical values on 2026-06-03 (prior catalog had size/hex length mismatch)

constants.name: md5_iv
constants.description: MD5 initial buffer A=0x67452301, B=0xefcdab89, C=0x98badcfe, D=0x10325476.

constants.name: aes_sbox
constants.description: AES Rijndael S-box (full 256 bytes); only first 16 stored for matching.  Inverse affine transformation over GF(2^8) of the multiplicative inverse.

constants.name: aes_inv_sbox
constants.description: AES Rijndael inverse S-box used by InvSubBytes() during decryption.

constants.name: chacha20_constant
constants.description: ChaCha20 sigma constant occupying the first 4 words of the initial 4x4 state.
constants.spec_citation: RFC 7539 §2.3 (The ChaCha20 Block Function — initial state)

constants.name: salsa20_constant
constants.description: Salsa20 32-byte-key sigma constant occupying state words [0,5,10,15] of the 4x4 state matrix.
constants.spec_citation: Bernstein, 'The Salsa20 family of stream ciphers' (2008) §2 — sigma constants

constants.name: salsa20_constant_short
constants.description: Salsa20 16-byte-key tau constant (short-key variant) used when the key is 128-bit instead of 256-bit.
constants.spec_citation: Bernstein, 'The Salsa20 family of stream ciphers' (2008) §2 — tau constants for 128-bit keys

constants.name: blake2b_iv
constants.description: BLAKE2b initial chaining values IV[0..1] (first two 64-bit words; identical to SHA-512 IV[0..1]).

constants.name: rsa_pkcs_oid_sha256
constants.description: DigestInfo prefix for RSA-PKCS1 signing with SHA-256 (DER-encoded AlgorithmIdentifier for id-sha256 plus OCTET-STRING tag).

constants.name: wanacry_magic
constants.description: WannaCry encrypted-file header magic; precedes the 4-byte AES-key blob length and the 256-byte RSA-encrypted AES-128 key.
constants.spec_citation: Sophos (Secureworks origin) 'wcry-ransomware-analysis' Figure 7-8 — WCry file header prepended to encrypted file. Cross-verified via aguinet/wannakey + gentilkiwi/wanakiwi decryptor source (existence of WCry file header indicator).
constants._verification_note: L1/L3 K-phase fetch-verify: original logrhythm URL 301-redirected to exabeam homepage (article deleted). Replaced with Sophos analysis (Figure 7-8 WCry file header, page alive). Well-known fact cross-cited by 3 public decryptor implementations.

constants.name: ms_cryptoapi_priv_blob_magic
constants.description: Microsoft CryptoAPI PRIVATEKEYBLOB magic 'RSA2' (LE 0x32415352) preceding the 8-byte BLOBHEADER's RSA component.
constants.spec_citation: Microsoft Learn — 'Base Provider Key BLOBs' (PRIVATEKEYBLOB / PUBLICKEYBLOB structure)

constants.name: ms_cryptoapi_pub_blob_magic
constants.description: Microsoft CryptoAPI PUBLICKEYBLOB magic 'RSA1' (LE 0x31415352) inside RSAPUBKEY structure.
constants.spec_citation: Microsoft Learn — 'Base Provider Key BLOBs' (PUBLICKEYBLOB structure)

constants.name: cng_rsa_priv_full
constants.description: CNG (BCrypt) RSA private full BLOB magic 'RSA3' carrying P, Q, dP, dQ, InvQ in addition to the public components.

constants.name: ecc_priv_p256
constants.description: CNG (BCrypt) ECDSA P-256 private BLOB magic 'ECS2' = BCRYPT_ECDSA_PRIVATE_P256_MAGIC (0x32534345).
constants.spec_citation: Microsoft Learn — 'BCRYPT_ECCKEY_BLOB' Magic field for ECC P-256 private key

constants.name: tea_delta
constants.description: TEA delta = sqrt(5)*2^31 = 0x9E3779B9 — added to round counter every encrypt round (Wheeler-Needham FSE 1994 §3).  Same constant appears in XTEA, XXTEA, Blowfish key-schedule variants.
constants.spec_citation: Wheeler & Needham, TEA: Tiny Encryption Algorithm (FSE 1994, Springer LNCS 1008, §3)
constants.ambiguous_reason: 0x9E3779B9 (golden ratio) is shared by TEA/XTEA/XXTEA/Serpent/RC5/RC6/SEED key-schedule and is also used by many non-crypto hash functions (Fibonacci hashing, splittable_random, etc.); requires family disambiguation before being attributed to a specific cipher.

constants.name: aes_rcon
constants.description: AES Rcon (round constants) used in key expansion: 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20, 0x40, 0x80, 0x1b, 0x36, ... (xtimes of 1 in GF(2^8) under the Rijndael polynomial). Often stored as a 10-byte table for AES-128 (10 rounds) or longer for AES-256. Extended sequence covers AES-128/192/256 round constants (per Crypto++ AES Tables rcon array). FIPS-197 AES-128 only uses first 10.
constants.spec_citation: FIPS-197 §5.2 (Key Expansion), 0x01..0x36 round constants for AES-128 (Rcon[1..10])

constants.name: hmac_ipad
constants.description: HMAC inner padding constant 0x36 (repeated). Block size depends on hash: 64 B for HMAC-SHA-1/-SHA-256, 128 B for HMAC-SHA-512. Common in KDF chains.

constants.name: hmac_opad
constants.description: HMAC outer padding constant 0x5c (repeated). Pair with hmac_ipad to confirm HMAC use.

constants.name: curve25519_basepoint
constants.description: X25519/Curve25519 base point u-coordinate = 9 (32-byte little-endian). Used as the public key generator in modern RaaS (Conti, BlackCat, Embargo, LockBit 3.0).

constants.name: sha1_iv
constants.description: SHA-1 initial hash values H0..H4 in big-endian byte order; rare in modern ransomware but appears in legacy CryptoAPI samples. (bytes corrected 2026-05-20: canonical FIPS-180-4 H0..H4).

constants.name: lockbit3_magic
constants.description: LockBit 3.0 (Black) ransom note + signature header tag. Commonly seen in encrypted file footer along with an RSA-2048-wrapped AES-256 file key (Sophos/Trend Micro RE 2022; earlier draft of this description incorrectly cited ChaCha20+Curve25519 — corrected 2026-05-29).

constants.name: conti_chacha8_constant
constants.description: Conti uses ChaCha8 (8-round variant) with the same expand-32 constant as ChaCha20.  Distinguishing factor is the loop count; the constant alone matches both.  Pair detection with quarter-round count (8 vs 20).
constants.spec_citation: Bernstein, ChaCha (2008) — Conti CTI: SophosLabs Uncut, Sep 2021

constants.name: sha224_iv
constants.description: SHA-224 initial hash values H0..H7 (FIPS-180-4)
constants.spec_citation: NIST FIPS 180-4 Sec 5.3.2 (SHA-224 initial hash values H0..H7)
constants._note: Regenerated from NIST FIPS 180-4 canonical values on 2026-06-03 (prior catalog had size/hex length mismatch)

constants.name: sha384_iv
constants.description: SHA-384 initial hash values H0..H7 per FIPS-180-4 §5.3.4.

constants.name: sha256_k_first16
constants.description: First 4 round constants K[0..3] of SHA-256
constants.spec_citation: NIST FIPS 180-4 Sec 4.2.2 (SHA-256 round constants K0..K3)
constants._note: Regenerated from NIST FIPS 180-4 canonical values on 2026-06-03 (prior catalog had size/hex length mismatch)

constants.name: md5_t_first16
constants.description: First 4 T[i] constants of MD5 (RFC-1321)

constants.name: ripemd160_iv
constants.description: RIPEMD-160 initial hash values

constants.name: blake2s_iv
constants.description: BLAKE2s initial vector (RFC-7693)

constants.name: keccak_round_constant_0
constants.description: First Keccak-f round constant RC[0] (FIPS-202)

constants.name: aes_rcon_first9
constants.description: AES key-schedule round constants Rcon[1..9]

constants.name: aes_te0_first16
constants.description: First 4 entries of T-table Te0 used by table-driven AES (Rijndael reference).

constants.name: aes_td0_first16
constants.description: First 4 entries of inverse T-table Td0 (Rijndael reference).

constants.name: twofish_q0_first16
constants.description: First 16 bytes of Twofish q0 permutation table per Schneier reference C TABLE.H P8x8[0][0..15].

constants.name: twofish_q1_first16
constants.description: First 16 bytes of Twofish q1 permutation table per Schneier reference C TABLE.H P8x8[1][0..15].

constants.name: serpent_phi_constant
constants.description: Serpent key-schedule golden ratio constant 0x9E3779B9 (little-endian)
constants.ambiguous_reason: 0x9E3779B9 golden-ratio word is shared with TEA, XTEA, RC5, RC6, SEED, Twofish, Boost hash_combine, LZ4, xxhash, and Java/JVM hashing. Single hit cannot uniquely attribute Serpent; family disambiguation required.

constants.name: blowfish_p_first16
constants.description: First 4 entries of Blowfish P-array (digits of pi)

constants.name: des_sbox_s1_first16
constants.description: DES S-box S1 row 0 (16 four-bit outputs, one byte each) per FIPS-46-3

constants.name: rc5_p32
constants.description: RC5 magic constant P32 = 0xB7E15163 (little-endian)

constants.name: rc5_q32
constants.description: RC5 magic constant Q32 = 0x9E3779B9 (little-endian)
constants.ambiguous_reason: 0x9E3779B9 shared with TEA/XTEA/Serpent/RC6/SEED key-schedule; family disambiguation required.

constants.name: rc6_p32
constants.description: RC6 magic constant P32 = 0xB7E15163 = Odd((e-2)*2^32). Identical to RC5 P32 by design (Rivest-Robshaw-Sidney-Yin 1998 reused RC5 key-expansion). Widely used by RC6 ransomware variants.
constants.spec_citation: RFC 2040 §5.1 (RC5 spec defines Pw=Odd((e-2)*2^w); RC6 spec [Rivest-Robshaw-Sidney-Yin 1998] reuses identical RC5 key-expansion constants)
constants._secondary_source: Added Wikipedia RC5 (alive, directly quotes Pw=Odd((e-2)*2^w) formula) + RSA Labs RRSY98 RC6 paper PDF (Rivest et al 1998) as secondary corroborating sources.

constants.name: rc6_q32
constants.description: RC6 magic constant Q32 = 0x9E3779B9 = Odd((phi-1)*2^32). Identical to RC5 Q32 by design (Rivest-Robshaw-Sidney-Yin 1998 reused RC5 key-expansion).
constants.spec_citation: RFC 2040 §5.1 (RC5 spec defines Qw=Odd((phi-1)*2^w); RC6 spec [Rivest-Robshaw-Sidney-Yin 1998] reuses identical RC5 key-expansion constants)
constants.ambiguous_reason: 0x9E3779B9 shared with TEA/XTEA/Serpent/RC5/SEED key-schedule; family disambiguation required.

constants.name: skipjack_F_first16
constants.description: First 16 bytes of Skipjack F-table

constants.name: camellia_sigma1
constants.description: Camellia key-schedule constant Sigma1

constants.name: camellia_sigma2
constants.description: Camellia key-schedule constant Sigma2

constants.name: aria_C1
constants.description: ARIA round constant C1

constants.name: seed_kc1
constants.description: SEED key-schedule constant KC1 (= KC0 rotated left 1 bit; KC0 is the golden-ratio 0x9E3779B9)
constants.ambiguous_reason: 0x9E3779B9 is the golden-ratio constant shared by TEA/XTEA/Serpent/RC5/RC6/SEED key-schedule and Fibonacci hashing; family disambiguation required.

constants.name: poly1305_clamp_mask
constants.description: Poly1305 r-value clamping mask (RFC-7539): 0x0ffffffc 0x0fffffff x3 packed

constants.name: chacha20_constant_le_split
constants.description: ChaCha20/Salsa20 constants as four 32-bit little-endian words: 'expa','nd 3','2-by','te k'

constants.name: lockbit_3_marker
constants.description: Common ransom-note string marker for LockBit family

constants.name: babuk_marker
constants.ascii: choung dong looks like hot dog!!
constants.description: Babuk encrypted-file footer/header marker (32 bytes; added trailing '!' so marker ends '...dog!!' per canonical Babuk samples; prior 31-byte form ended in single '!').

constants.name: ryuk_marker
constants.description: Hermes/Ryuk encrypted-file marker (Ryuk is Hermes-derived)

constants.name: petya_verification_fill
constants.description: Petya verification block is 0x37-filled (per Kaspersky Securelist Petya analysis).
constants.ambiguous_reason: 0x37-repeat pattern is low-specificity; only meaningful when found at MBR sector 55 offset with surrounding Petya disk layout.

constants.name: stop_djvu_salt
constants.description: STOP/Djvu hardcoded salt-like GUID prefix used in offline-key fallback

constants.name: 7z_aes_signature
constants.description: 7-Zip archive magic; combined with AES-256 header property 0x06F10701 indicates 7zAES

constants.name: 7z_aes_property_id
constants.description: 7-Zip method-ID for AES-256-SHA256 (7zAES)

constants.name: kuznyechik_pi_first16
constants.description: First 16 bytes of GOST Kuznyechik nonlinear S-box (some EU/RU samples)

constants.name: argon2_blake2b_init
constants.description: Argon2 reuses BLAKE2b IV; presence + Argon2 string indicates Argon2 KDF

constants.name: scrypt_blockmix_constant
constants.description: scrypt context label string; appears in some libraries' KDF context

constants.name: pbkdf2_label_default
constants.description: PBKDF2 label string (some implementations include this in context)

constants.name: openssl_salted_magic
constants.description: OpenSSL CLI 'enc' container magic; often appears in malware that wraps with `openssl enc`

constants.name: ssh_aes256_ctr_marker
constants.description: Cipher-name marker present in OpenSSH-style key blobs

constants.name: calg_des
constants.description: Microsoft CryptoAPI ALG_ID CALG_DES = 0x6601 (LE: 01 66 00 00).

constants.name: calg_aes_128
constants.description: Microsoft CryptoAPI CALG_AES_128 = 0x660E (little-endian)

constants.name: calg_aes_192
constants.description: Microsoft CryptoAPI CALG_AES_192 = 0x660F (little-endian)

constants.description: Microsoft CryptoAPI CALG_AES_256 = 0x6610 (little-endian)

constants.description: Microsoft CryptoAPI CALG_RC4 = 0x6801 (little-endian)

constants.name: calg_rsa_keyx
constants.description: Microsoft CryptoAPI CALG_RSA_KEYX = 0xA400 (little-endian)

constants.name: salsa20_constant_tau
constants.description: Salsa20 'tau' constant for 128-bit keys (already in baseline; included for completeness with explicit name)

constants.name: aes_sbox_first16
constants.description: AES forward S-box (SubBytes) first 16 bytes -- row 0 of the substitution table.  Distinct from aes_invsbox_first16 which is the inverse S-box used for AES decryption.

constants.name: aes_invsbox_first16
constants.description: AES inverse S-box (Rijndael InvSubBytes table) first 16 bytes. Distinct from Td0 (T-table); appears in byte-by-byte AES decryption code that does not use AES-NI or T-tables (typical fallback paths in OpenSSL no-AESNI builds, mbedTLS legacy, hand-rolled implementations).

constants.name: ms_cryptoapi_privatekeyblob_rsa1024_header
constants.description: MS CryptoAPI PUBLICKEYSTRUC + RSAPUBKEY header prefix for a PRIVATEKEYBLOB exporting an RSA-1024 keyx key. bType=0x07 (PRIVATEKEYBLOB), bVersion=0x02, reserved=0x0000, aiKeyAlg=CALG_RSA_KEYX (0x0000A400 LE). Found at offset 0 of any blob produced by CryptExportKey(PRIVATEKEYBLOB, ...) for a CALG_RSA_KEYX key.

constants.name: cng_bcrypt_rsaprivate_blob_magic
constants.description: CNG BCRYPT_RSAPRIVATE_BLOB magic ('RSA2'). First 4 bytes of any blob produced by BCryptExportKey with the BCRYPT_RSAPRIVATE_BLOB type. Distinguishes from BCRYPT_RSAFULLPRIVATE_BLOB (RSA3) by the absence of CRT parameters (P, Q, dP, dQ, InvQ).

constants.name: cng_bcrypt_rsafullprivate_blob_magic
constants.description: CNG BCRYPT_RSAFULLPRIVATE_BLOB magic ('RSA3'). Full RSA private key including CRT parameters; produced when an attacker exports a key with BCRYPT_RSAFULLPRIVATE_BLOB. Sufficient for direct decryption (no need to reconstruct CRT params).

constants.name: salsa20_constant_sigma
constants.description: Salsa20 'sigma' constant for 256-bit keys (the 32-byte-key variant - more common than tau in modern code; used by WannaCry's secondary cipher path, EKANS/Snake, several Conti forks).

constants.name: bcrypt_aes_algorithm_utf16
constants.description: BCRYPT_AES_ALGORITHM identifier as a UTF-16LE null-terminated wide string. Passed to BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider(... L"AES" ...). Found in .rdata of every binary that uses CNG AES through the documented API path. Strong indicator of CNG-based AES use even when the API itself is statically resolved.

constants.name: bcrypt_rsa_algorithm_utf16
constants.description: BCRYPT_RSA_ALGORITHM identifier as a UTF-16LE null-terminated wide string. Passed to BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider(... L"RSA" ...). Same role as bcrypt_aes_algorithm_utf16 but for RSA.

constants.name: openssl_rsa_no_padding
constants.description: OpenSSL RSA_NO_PADDING = 3. No padding (raw RSA — sometimes used by malware)

constants.name: openssl_rsa_pkcs1_oaep_padding
constants.description: OpenSSL RSA_PKCS1_OAEP_PADDING = 4. OAEP padding (HOT — modern ransomware)
constants.ambiguous_reason: 4-byte LE 0x04000000 is just integer=4 and matches any program that stores int=4 in memory; must be corroborated by RSA modulus length or OpenSSL EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_rsa_padding API trace before counting as smoking gun.

constants.name: openssl_rsa_x931_padding
constants.description: OpenSSL RSA_X931_PADDING = 5. X9.31 padding

constants.name: openssl_rsa_pkcs1_pss_padding
constants.description: OpenSSL RSA_PKCS1_PSS_PADDING = 6. PSS padding

constants.name: openssl_rsa_pkcs1_with_tls_padding
constants.description: OpenSSL RSA_PKCS1_WITH_TLS_PADDING = 7. PKCS#1 with TLS-style padding (constant-time)

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_pbkdf2
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("PBKDF2"). PKCS#5 PBKDF2 — pass to EVP_KDF_fetch (HOT — password-based ransomware)

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_scrypt
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("SCRYPT"). scrypt — pass to EVP_KDF_fetch

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_hkdf
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("HKDF"). HKDF (RFC 5869) — pass to EVP_KDF_fetch

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_tls1_prf
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("TLS1-PRF"). TLS 1.0/1.1 PRF

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_kbkdf
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("KBKDF"). SP800-108 KBKDF

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_krb5kdf
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("KRB5KDF"). Kerberos 5 KDF

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_x942kdf
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("X942KDF"). X9.42 KDF

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_x963kdf
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("X963KDF"). X9.63 KDF (used after ECDH)

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_sshkdf
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("SSHKDF"). SSH KDF

constants.name: openssl_kdf_fetch_sskdf
constants.description: String passed to EVP_KDF_fetch("SSKDF"). SP800-56C single-step (SSKDF).

self_prng_indicators.name: rdtsc_seed
self_prng_indicators.context: Read time-stamp counter; used as PRNG seed by Conti, LockBit and many cobbled-together stream-cipher implementations.

self_prng_indicators.name: rdtscp_seed
self_prng_indicators.context: Variant of rdtsc with serializing semantics; same intent.

self_prng_indicators.name: QueryPerformanceCounter
self_prng_indicators.context: High-resolution timer used as RNG seed in many in-house ransomware PRNGs.

self_prng_indicators.name: QueryPerformanceFrequency
self_prng_indicators.context: Often called alongside QueryPerformanceCounter as a seed mixer.

self_prng_indicators.name: GetTickCount
self_prng_indicators.context: Low-resolution timer used as a weak seed; classic ransomware fingerprint.

self_prng_indicators.name: time_c_runtime
self_prng_indicators.context: C runtime time(0) seed. Strong indicator of weak PRNG when followed by srand+rand.

self_prng_indicators.name: srand
self_prng_indicators.context: Seeding the C runtime PRNG; rand() output should NEVER be the source of cryptographic keys, but several ransomware families do exactly that.

self_prng_indicators.name: rand_s
self_prng_indicators.context: rand_s is the cryptographically-secure variant on Windows; presence does NOT indicate weak PRNG, but co-occurrence with rand() patterns is informative.

self_prng_indicators.name: GetCurrentThreadId
self_prng_indicators.context: Used as additional seed entropy by simple in-house PRNGs.

self_prng_indicators.name: GetComputerNameA
self_prng_indicators.context: Commonly mixed into per-machine 'unique' victim ID PRNG.

self_prng_indicators.name: GetVolumeInformationA
self_prng_indicators.context: Volume serial number used in ID/key-derivation in several families (CryptoLocker derivatives).

self_prng_indicators.name: Linear-congruential-multiplier-1103515245
self_prng_indicators.context: Classic LCG multiplier (1103515245); appears in glibc-style rand() and copies.

self_prng_indicators.name: MSVC-rand-multiplier-214013
self_prng_indicators.context: MSVC rand() LCG multiplier 214013 (=0x343FD); strong indicator of MS C runtime rand().

self_prng_indicators.name: Mersenne-twister-init-1812433253
self_prng_indicators.context: MT19937 initialization multiplier 1812433253; presence indicates self-built MT.

self_prng_indicators.name: xorshift32-magic-2147483647
self_prng_indicators.context: Common xorshift mask; weak by itself but combined with shift-13/17/5 patterns is diagnostic.

self_prng_indicators.name: CryptoAPI-CSP-default-string
self_prng_indicators.context: Many ransomware families that use legacy CryptoAPI explicitly request this CSP.

self_prng_indicators.name: CryptoAPI-CSP-RSA-AES-string
self_prng_indicators.pattern: Microsoft Enhanced RSA and AES Cryptographic Provider

self_prng_indicators.name: RDRAND-instruction
self_prng_indicators.context: Hardware RNG; modern ransomware sometimes uses it directly.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: 16-byte_imm_aligned_in_rdata
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: A 16-byte block at .rdata aligned address that is later loaded into AES key schedule via mov xmm0,[mem]; movdqu/aesenc.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: 32-byte_imm_aligned_in_rdata
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: A 32-byte block at .rdata aligned address consumed by AES-256 key schedule or ChaCha20 key load.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: RSA-public-key-blob-in-rdata
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: A static RSA modulus (256/512 bytes) plus a 4-byte public exponent (0x00010001) embedded in .rdata; classic 'attacker public key shipped in binary' pattern.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: RSA-public-exponent-65537
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: Public exponent e=65537 in little-endian (01 00 01 00). Combined with a contiguous 256/512-byte modulus is a strong attacker-pubkey indicator.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: Curve25519-pubkey-32B-in-rdata
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: 32 contiguous bytes treated as an X25519 public key; appears in BlackCat/ALPHV, Sodinokibi/REvil drop variants.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: high-entropy-32B-block-multiple-references
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: 32-byte block in .rdata referenced from multiple call sites and never written; classical hardcoded master key.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: ASCII-key-string
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: ASCII string of length 16/24/32 stored as a literal and passed to AES_set_encrypt_key / EVP_EncryptInit_ex / mbedtls_aes_setkey_enc.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: RC4-key-string-shorter-than-32
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: ASCII/printable string 5-31 bytes long, passed to RC4_set_key/CryptDeriveKey for legacy CryptoAPI RC4 (CryptoLocker, early Cerber variants).

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: static-IV-zero16
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: 16 bytes of NULs used as IV; common in WannaCry-style AES-CBC.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: static-IV-counter-pattern
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: 16-byte block where the last 4-8 bytes look like a counter (incrementing) — typical AES-CTR fixed-nonce error mode used by some samples.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: ChaCha20-key-and-nonce-12B-pair
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: A 32-byte block (key) immediately followed by a 12-byte block (RFC-7539 nonce) in .rdata: indicates hardcoded ChaCha20 keying.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: Salsa20-key-and-nonce-8B-pair
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: A 32-byte key followed by an 8-byte nonce — original Salsa20 nonce length, used by older STOP/Djvu variants.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: BCRYPT_RSAFULLPRIVATE_BLOB-in-rdata
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: Static private key shipped in the binary (debug builds, unwrapped Conti/REvil dumps).

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: Hardcoded-AES-S-box-followed-by-key
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: If the AES S-box is statically embedded (i.e., custom AES instead of AES-NI) and a 16/32-byte key candidate sits nearby, treat key as hardcoded.

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: Single-XOR-byte-key
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: A loop body 'xor byte ptr [rsi], 0xNN' with a constant immediate is a single-byte XOR cipher (very weak; used by joke/wiper variants).

hardcoded_key_indicators.name: 32-byte-XOR-key-rotated
hardcoded_key_indicators.context: Loop body 'xor byte ptr [rsi+rcx], byte ptr [key+rcx & 31]' = repeating 32B XOR key; trivially recoverable.
